method: Blender MCP: Python MCP stdio client -> uvx blender-mcp -> installed Blender addon, localhost:9876. All three PNGs rendered inside the GUI Blender session; background Blender was used only for API probing and saved-file validation.
renderer: Cycles, Metal GPU, Apple M1 Max; 160 samples with denoising

visual_review.hero: Inspected final render: full island and buildings fit frame; two cream hooded seated avatars face the central fire; dark navy cafe silhouettes, six chairs, two tables and cups; orange/yellow faceted fire and rising embers.
visual_review.ember_split: Inspected final render: the shared ember separates into two curved, broken trails with bright arrival embers at the two phones.
visual_review.cold_open: Diorama placed at right; left title space uses a subtle irregular concentric grain motif. Final revised output inspected before delivery.

lighting: One point light at the fire plus emissive fire, coals and embers. Zero world illumination; no fill, rim, sun or area lights. Non-fire materials have a camera-ray-only base-color floor for the specified flat palette; this casts no light on other objects.

issues.issue: MCP client expects addon protocol 15; installed addon reports protocol 5.
issues.resolution: Existing execute-code API worked. No addon replacement or persistent global MCP configuration change was needed.

issues.issue: Blender 5.2 moved glare controls to node input sockets; first attempt using glare_type failed and produced a black preliminary preview.
issues.resolution: Probed installed RNA and socket values, changed to Type='Fog Glow' and Quality='High', repaired node links, and inspected regenerated PNGs.

issues.issue: First artwork preview clipped building tops and overexposed the warm light.
issues.resolution: Widened orthographic framing, lowered fire light, and applied a camera-only flat base-color floor.

issues.issue: First cold-open framing placed the title area on the opposite side from the intended layout.
issues.resolution: Corrected the camera-right vector sign and rerendered the cold-open scene.

provenance: Locally authored procedural meshes, curves and materials. No external assets, textures, paid generation or external asset licenses.
validation: validation.json records readback of the final saved blend, per-scene object counts, light configuration, compositor scene links, decoded PNG sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
